briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF S-011
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- water tower top: (10, -80), roof
- control room: (-135, -70), indoor
- site B: (-79, 133), outdoor
- water tank: (145, -44), outdoor

Robots:
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 6.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg). Endurance: 1020 s, including the return to its start.
- D2 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 8.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg), thermal camera. Endurance: 1140 s, including the return to its start.
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 8 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 2760 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Collect a soil sample (1 kg) at site B and keep it on board. Location: site B. Duration: 90 s. Needs: robotic arm, cargo carrier (payload 1 kg).
- T2: Inspect water tower top with a camera. Location: water tower top. Duration: 150 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 300 s.
- T3: Inspect water tower top with a camera. Location: water tower top. Duration: 60 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 300 s.
- T4: Collect a soil sample (3 kg) at site B and keep it on board. Location: site B. Duration: 90 s. Needs: robotic arm, cargo carrier (payload 3 kg).
- T5: Tighten the valve at water tank. Location: water tank. Duration: 210 s. Needs: robotic arm.

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Keep at least 1 quadcopter on standby: it must not be given any task.
6. Every task must be finished by t = 1500 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Morning! Plan for today's site work:

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: water tower top (10, -80, a rooftop); control room (-135, -70, indoors); site B (-79, 133, outside); water tank (145, -44, outside).

The fleet: D1 is a quadcopter at base with a camera; it flies at 6.5 m/s, can lift 2 kg, and its battery lasts 17 minutes including the flight home. D2 is a quadcopter at base with a camera and a thermal camera; it flies at 8.5 m/s, can lift 2 kg, and its battery lasts 19 minutes including the flight home. M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 8 kg, moves at 1 m/s and lasts 46 minutes including getting back.

Jobs:
(T1) Pick up a soil sample at site B and keep it on board; it weighs 1 kg - that takes 1.5 minutes on site.
(T2) Get eyes on water tower top and check the panels - that takes 2.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 5 minutes.
(T3) Have a look at water tower top - that takes 1 minute on site and it has to be finished within the first 5 minutes.
(T4) Pick up a soil sample at site B and keep it on board; it weighs 3 kg - that takes 1.5 minutes on site.
(T5) The valve at water tank needs tightening - that takes 3.5 minutes on site.

Keep one quadcopter on standby; don't give it any jobs. Everything has to be wrapped up within 25 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
